findings.finding: Capable expert composition with the same methods, information, reusable templates, scientific output and review is the comparator. No product premium is justified by withholding tools from that baseline.

Initial/shared/marginal costs, unsuccessful work, adoption timing, review, data, compute, integration, recovery and institutional participation are distinct. Missing actual prices remain null. USD, USD-million and CNY examples are separate.

Low/moderate reuse and the adoption ramp lose under the assumed account. Marginal savings and shared-cost sensitivities, harmful decisions, correlated tasks, unsupported causal truth and hard constraints are explicit.

EVSI compares the best action before/after information and subtracts information cost separately. The 8000-cost study has negative assumed net value; failure denominators, irrelevant information, correlated answers and finite stopping are developed.

Start with matched public/generated tasks and explicit acquisition/compute budgets; compare fixed/random/numerical and optional model-assisted decisions, including clean and failed cases. Bank measurement follows only if prototype evidence reveals a decision-changing unresolved variable and plausible positive net information value.
No measured bank ROI, adoption, labor substitution, vendor quotation or calibrated bank signal likelihood is asserted. Runtime measurements are explicitly separated from labor value.
